---
    [".oh-my-bash".clone]
        args = ["--depth", "1"]
    [".oh-my-bash".pull]
        args = ["--ff-only"]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ble.sh (Bash Line Editor; all platforms; bash 4.0+)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Provides zsh-style autosuggestions / syntax-highlighting / vi-mode for bash.
# Init order in dot_bashrc.tmpl is load-bearing — see the 12-step header
# comment there. Compiled artefact lives at ~/.local/share/blesh/ble.sh,
# regenerated by `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_25_install_blesh
# .sh.tmpl` whenever the source clone HEAD changes.
#
# Submodules: ble.sh depends on a `contrib` submodule that ships extras
# (color themes, integration helpers). The upstream README explicitly
# recommends `git clone --recursive`; we pass --recurse-submodules to the
# clone and --recurse-submodules to the pull so the submodule tree stays
# fresh on the weekly refresh.

[".local/share/blesh"]
    type = "git-repo"
    url = "https://github.com/akinomyoga/ble.sh.git"
    refreshPeriod = "168h"
    [".local/share/blesh".clone]
        args = ["--depth", "1", "--recurse-submodules", "--shallow-submodules"]
    [".local/share/blesh".pull]
        args = ["--ff-only", "--recurse-submodules"]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# TPM (Tmux Plugin Manager) -- all platforms
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The `tpm install_plugins` step that populates ~/.tmux/plugins/* stays in
# the ansible `devtools` role (it needs a running tmux + the tmux config).

[".tmux/plugins/tpm"]
    type = "git-repo"
    url = "https://github.com/tmux-plugins/tpm.git"
    refreshPeriod = "168h"
    [".tmux/plugins/tpm".clone]
        args = ["--depth", "1"]
    [".tmux/plugins/tpm".pull]
        args = ["--ff-only"]

{{ if ne .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# fzf (Linux only)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# macOS installs fzf via Homebrew (see roles/lazyvim_deps). On Linux the apt
# package is too old and lacks `--zsh`, so we clone upstream and let ansible
# run `~/.fzf/install --bin` to populate ~/.fzf/bin/fzf.

[".fzf"]
    type = "git-repo"
    url = "https://github.com/junegunn/fzf.git"
    refreshPeriod = "168h"

# Fix: `chezmoi update` blocked by dirty ble.sh clone

## Context

`chezmoi update` fails when it tries to refresh the ble.sh git-repo external:

\```
error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:
    lib/core-complete.sh  lib/core-syntax.sh  lib/init-term.sh ...
chezmoi: .local/share/blesh: ... exit status 1
\```

### Root cause — NOT our config, NOT agent-generated

It is **ble.sh's own `make install` mutating its git checkout.**

- `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` clones the source to `~/.local/share/blesh` (`type = "git-repo"`, weekly `pull --ff-only --recurse-submodules`).
- `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_26_install_blesh.sh.tmpl` runs `make -C ~/.local/share/blesh install PREFIX=$HOME/.local`.
- In ble.sh's `GNUmakefile`, `PREFIX=$HOME/.local` → `DATADIR=$HOME/.local/share` → **`INSDIR=$HOME/.local/share/blesh`** — i.e. the install destination is the **same directory as the git clone**.
- `make install` copies the *processed* build output (`out/lib/*.sh`: license header added, comments + blank lines stripped) **over the tracked source `lib/*.sh`**, plus writes untracked `licenses/`. This dirties the working tree (`git diff --stat`: 26 files, ~11k deletions).
- Next weekly refresh, chezmoi's `git pull --ff-only` refuses to overwrite the locally-modified tracked files → the error.

So the "local changes" are build artifacts, not anything we or an agent wrote. The structural bug is the **clone-path == install-PREFIX-target collision** (ble.sh expects these to differ).

## Immediate unblock (currently-broken machine)

Discard the build-mutated tracked files so the fast-forward pull can proceed, then finish the update:

\```
git -C ~/.local/share/blesh reset --hard
chezmoi apply --refresh-externals    # or re-run `chezmoi update`
\```

- **Decouple dirs (canonical)** - Clone ble.sh source to ~/.local/src/blesh and install into ~/.local/share/blesh (ble.sh's intended layout — install dir is a plain dir, never a git repo). Cleaner long-term, but needs a one-time rm of the old git dir on every host (a run_once migration).

Your questions have been answered: "How should I permanently stop ble.sh's `make install` from dirtying its git clone and blocking the weekly pull?"=(no option selected) notes: 我會選 **2. Decouple dirs（canonical）**。

核心原因：你真正的 root cause 是 **把 ble.sh 的 git clone 放在 install output 目錄裡**：

```text
~/.local/share/blesh   同時是 source checkout
~/.local/share/blesh   又是 make install 的 runtime output
```

所以 `make install` 會把 generated/runtime 檔案寫進 git worktree，導致 chezmoi weekly pull/update 時看到 dirty tree。

方案 1 的 `git reset --hard` 是止血，不是根治。它的問題是：

```bash
git reset --hard
```

只會還原 tracked files，**不會清掉 untracked/generated files**。如果 dirty 來源包含 `ble.sh`、`out/` 這類 generated artifact，通常還要 `git clean`，但那又更危險，可能把 local debug/build cache 一起清掉。

比較理想的結構會變成：

```text
~/.local/src/blesh        # git repo，只負責 pull/update/build source
~/.local/share/blesh      # runtime install output，不是 git repo
```

這樣 `chezmoi update` 管的是乾淨 source repo，`make install` 產物則落到 runtime path。

---

## 但 migration 要保守

特別是這段一定要加條件，不要無腦刪：

```bash
old="$HOME/.local/share/blesh"

fi
```

因為只有當舊的 `~/.local/share/blesh` 是 git clone 時才刪。之後它會變成正常 runtime install 目錄，就不應該再被 migration script 刪掉。

如果主要是 untracked/generated files，`reset --hard` 可能不夠。

## Approved Plan:
# Fix: `chezmoi update` blocked by dirty ble.sh clone

## Context

`chezmoi update` fails when it tries to refresh the ble.sh git-repo external:

```
error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:
    lib/core-complete.sh  lib/core-syntax.sh  lib/init-term.sh ...
chezmoi: .local/share/blesh: ... exit status 1
```

### Root cause — NOT our config, NOT agent-generated

It is **ble.sh's own `make install` mutating its git checkout.**

- `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` clones the source to `~/.local/share/blesh` (`type = "git-repo"`, weekly `pull --ff-only --recurse-submodules`).
- `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_26_install_blesh.sh.tmpl` runs `make -C ~/.local/share/blesh install PREFIX=$HOME/.local`.
- In ble.sh's `GNUmakefile`, `PREFIX=$HOME/.local` → `DATADIR=$HOME/.local/share` → **`INSDIR=$HOME/.local/share/blesh`** — i.e. the install destination is the **same directory as the git clone**.
- `make install` copies the *processed* build output (`out/lib/*.sh`: license header added, comments + blank lines stripped) **over the tracked source `lib/*.sh`**, plus writes untracked `licenses/`. This dirties the working tree (`git diff --stat`: 26 files, ~11k deletions).
- Next weekly refresh, chezmoi's `git pull --ff-only` refuses to overwrite the locally-modified tracked files → the error.

So the "local changes" are build artifacts, not anything we or an agent wrote. The structural bug is the **clone-path == install-PREFIX-target collision** (ble.sh expects these to differ).

## Permanent fix — Option 2: decouple source clone from install target (chosen)

ble.sh's intended layout: clone the source somewhere, then `make install PREFIX=~/.local` installs into `~/.local/share/blesh`. We currently put the clone *at* the install target, so `make install` writes over its own checkout. Fix = move the clone out of the install dir.

**New layout:**

```
~/.local/src/blesh     # git clone — source only; chezmoi pulls/updates here
~/.local/share/blesh   # make-install output (runtime) — NOT a git repo
```

The runtime artefact stays at `~/.local/share/blesh/ble.sh`, so **`dot_bashrc.tmpl` (lines 50/52) and all docs that reference that path need no changes** — only the source-clone location moves.

### Edits

**1. `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` (~lines 91-112)** — move the external from the install dir to a source dir:
- Rename the table key `[".local/share/blesh"]` → `[".local/src/blesh"]` (and its `.clone` / `.pull` subtables). Keep `type`, `url`, `refreshPeriod`, and the `--recurse-submodules` args identical.

```tmpl
#!/bin/bash
# One-time migration: ble.sh source clone moved out of its install dir.
#
# Old layout cloned the git repo straight into ~/.local/share/blesh, which is
# also `make install`'s INSDIR (from PREFIX=~/.local). The install rewrote the
# checkout's lib/*.sh in place, dirtying the tree so the weekly
# `git pull --ff-only` aborted ("local changes would be overwritten by merge").
# New layout: source clone -> ~/.local/src/blesh, runtime install ->
# ~/.local/share/blesh (a plain dir, no .git). See
# pitfalls/chezmoi-update-blesh-local-changes-overwritten.md.
#
# This runs in the `before` phase, ahead of the relocated external clone and
# the run_after_26 install, so the stale git repo is gone before `make install`
# repopulates ~/.local/share/blesh as a clean runtime dir.
#
# Guard: delete ONLY while it is still a git clone. Once migrated, the path is
# a normal install dir and must never be removed by this script.

set -e

old="$HOME/.local/share/blesh"

if [ -d "$old/.git" ]; then
    echo -e "\033[0;34m[INFO]\033[0m Migrating ble.sh: removing old git clone at $old (source moves to ~/.local/src/blesh)"
    rm -rf "$old"
fi

```

```

1	# Pitfalls
2	
3	Past traps we've stepped on. Symptoms-first knowledge base — the goal is that
4	when a problem recurs (on a new machine, after an upgrade, with a new tool
5	combo), grepping the symptom here lands you on the root cause and workaround
6	in seconds, instead of re-debugging from scratch.
7	
8	This folder is `chezmoi`-ignored (see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `pitfalls/**`); it
9	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
10	
11	## Pitfalls vs the rest
12	
13	This repo has four sibling surfaces with overlapping shapes; pick the right one:
14	
15	| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| `docs/tools/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
18	| `docs/this_repo/<topic>.md` | Present | "Why did we architect it this way?" | Read top to bottom |
19	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
20	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
21	| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |
22	
23	A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` when the trap is
24	serious enough that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it
25	recurs across machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround
26	is non-obvious and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a
27	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the invariant.
28	
29	## When to add a pitfall doc
30	
31	Add a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something
32	where the answer wasn't googleable, AND any of:
33	
34	- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (`SSH_CONNECTION` cleared
35	  silently → hostname module disappears, no error)
36	- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
37	  must come after `wait $pid` for fleet-apply, etc.)
38	- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
39	- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
40	- A specific tool version is required (or forbidden) and the failure mode at
41	  the wrong version is silent / confusing (e.g. tmux 3.2a popup off-screen)
42	
43	## When NOT to add a pitfall doc
44	
45	- Trivially googleable error (the next person will solve in 30 seconds anyway)
46	- Already covered in `docs/tools/<tool>.md` as part of the tool's normal
47	  configuration — cross-link from this README's "Cross-referenced pitfalls"
48	  table below instead of duplicating
49	- Already a `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant — those have higher priority enforcement
50	  (cross-link only)
51	- One-off transient (network glitch, machine-specific config rot) — fix and
52	  move on
53

```md
# `chezmoi update` aborts on ble.sh: "local changes would be overwritten by merge"

**Symptoms** (grep this section): `chezmoi update` / `chezmoi apply --refresh-externals` fails while refreshing the ble.sh git-repo external with:

\```
error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:
    lib/core-complete.sh
    lib/core-syntax.sh
    lib/init-term.sh
    lib/keymap.vi_digraph.sh
    lib/test-main.sh
    lib/test-util.sh
Please commit your changes or stash them before you merge.
Aborting
chezmoi: .local/share/blesh: /Users/<user>/.local/share/blesh: exit status 1
\```

`git -C ~/.local/share/blesh status` shows ~26 tracked `lib/*.sh` modified (a `git diff` reveals an added BSD-3-Clause license header + stripped comments/blank lines), plus untracked `licenses/`.

**First seen**: 2026-05
**Affects**: any host where the ble.sh source was cloned into `~/.local/share/blesh` AND `make install PREFIX=~/.local` ran there (the old chezmoi external layout). All OSes.
**Status**: fixed (source clone relocated to `~/.local/src/blesh`)

## Symptom

The weekly external refresh (`refreshPeriod = "168h"`, `pull --ff-only --recurse-submodules`) aborts because the working tree of `~/.local/share/blesh` is dirty. The "local changes" look mysterious — nobody edited ble.sh's source, and the diff is a wholesale rewrite (license header on, comments off) of files like `lib/core-syntax.sh`.

## Root cause

NOT user config, NOT agent-generated. It is **ble.sh's own `make install` overwriting its git checkout**, because the clone path and the install target were the same directory:

- chezmoi external cloned the source to `~/.local/share/blesh`.
- `run_onchange_after_26_install_blesh.sh.tmpl` ran `make -C ~/.local/share/blesh install PREFIX=$HOME/.local`.
- In ble.sh's `GNUmakefile`, `PREFIX=$HOME/.local` → `DATADIR=$HOME/.local/share` → **`INSDIR=$HOME/.local/share/blesh`** — identical to the clone.
- `make install` copies the *processed* build output (`out/lib/*.sh`, with license header + stripped comments) over the tracked source `lib/*.sh`, and writes untracked `licenses/`. The checkout is now dirty.
- Next `git pull --ff-only` refuses to clobber the locally-modified tracked files → the abort above.

ble.sh's documented usage clones the source somewhere and installs into a *separate* `PREFIX`; co-locating them is the trap.

## Workaround

Immediate unblock on a still-broken host (discards the build-mutated tracked files; untracked `licenses/` and submodule content don't block a fast-forward):

\```bash
git -C ~/.local/share/blesh reset --hard
chezmoi apply --refresh-externals   # or re-run `chezmoi update`
\```

This only re-arms the trap — the next install dirties the tree again. The permanent fix below removes the collision.

## Prevention

Decouple the source clone from the install target (the fix now in-repo):

- `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` clones to `[".local/src/blesh"]` (source only).
- `run_onchange_after_26_install_blesh.sh.tmpl` sets `BLESH_SRC="$HOME/.local/src/blesh"` and the HEAD-hash trigger reads `~/.local/src/blesh/.git/HEAD`; `make install PREFIX=$HOME/.local` still builds the runtime into `~/.local/share/blesh`, which is now a plain dir (no `.git`).
- `run_once_before_10_migrate_blesh_path.sh.tmpl` removes the old `~/.local/share/blesh` **only if it is still a git clone** (`[ -d "$old/.git" ]`), so `make install` repopulates a clean runtime dir.

The runtime artefact stays at `~/.local/share/blesh/ble.sh`, so `dot_bashrc.tmpl` and docs that source it are unchanged.

General rule: never point a build/install step's output dir at a chezmoi git-repo external's clone path — installers that rewrite tracked files in place will dirty the tree and break `pull --ff-only`.

## Related

- `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` (ble.sh block) — the decoupled layout + WHY comment.
- `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_26_install_blesh.sh.tmpl` — build-from-src.
- `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_once_before_10_migrate_blesh_path.sh.tmpl` — migration.
- [`pitfalls/blesh-set-v-leaks-gexec-wrapper.md`](blesh-set-v-leaks-gexec-wrapper.md) — other ble.sh trap.
- `docs/shells/bash.md` — ble.sh init order (12-step).
- Upstream: <https://github.com/akinomyoga/ble.sh> (install docs use a separate clone vs PREFIX).

# So we clone the SOURCE to ~/.local/src/blesh (pulled clean here) and let
# the install script build into the runtime dir ~/.local/share/blesh.
#
# Submodules: ble.sh depends on a `contrib` submodule that ships extras
# (color themes, integration helpers). The upstream README explicitly
# recommends `git clone --recursive`; we pass --recurse-submodules to the
# clone and --recurse-submodules to the pull so the submodule tree stays
--
[".local/src/blesh"]
    type = "git-repo"
    url = "https://github.com/akinomyoga/ble.sh.git"
    refreshPeriod = "168h"
rc=0
```

+- [ ] **[?/M] `opencodebox` wrapper for the containerized opencode image** — opencode's startup-tip suggests `docker run -it --rm ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode` for sandboxed runs, but the raw invocation is awkward (no cwd mount, no auth share, hits the Alpine/glibc OpenTUI loader bug on first run — see [pitfall](pitfalls/opencode-docker-opentui-glibc-loader-missing.md)). A thin wrapper (`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_opencodebox` Python uv-script, or a shell function in `dot_config/shell/`) would auto-mount `$PWD`:/workspace + `~/.local/share/opencode` (auth/sessions), forward TTY/COLOR/term env, apply the `apk add gcompat` workaround (or pin a `:debian` tag if upstream publishes one), and expose `--no-net` / `--ro` toggles. Useful for (a) sandboxed agent runs where the agent might `rm -rf` something, (b) CI / one-shot tasks, (c) trying opencode on a host without the native CLI installed. Native install (the just-shipped official-installer path in `coding_agents`) stays primary because the image has none of our mise/uv/cargo/brew tooling — only worth building if the container use case actually shows up. Two design splits: lightweight (shell function, dispatches `gcompat`-installing variant tag when present) vs full (Python script alongside `fleet` / `mlf` / `pqsum`, with completion + AGENTS.md row). → [research](backlog/opencodebox-wrapper.md)

## Done. Cause + fix summary

**The cause was neither your config nor an agent** — it was **ble.sh's own `make install` overwriting its git checkout**. The clone lived at `~/.local/share/blesh`, and `make install PREFIX=~/.local` resolves its install dir (`INSDIR`) to that *same* path. So every install rewrote the tracked `lib/*.sh` in place (license header added, comments stripped), dirtying the tree — and the next weekly `git pull --ff-only` refused to clobber those "local changes".

**Fix (your chosen Option 2 — decouple source from install target):**

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl` | external moved `[".local/share/blesh"]` → `[".local/src/blesh"]`; comment explains the WHY + fixed stale script-name `25`→`26` |
| `run_onchange_after_26_install_blesh.sh.tmpl` | `BLESH_SRC` + HEAD-hash trigger → `~/.local/src/blesh`; `make install PREFIX=~/.local` still builds runtime into `~/.local/share/blesh` (now a plain dir) |
| `run_once_before_10_migrate_blesh_path.sh.tmpl` (new) | `rm -rf ~/.local/share/blesh` **only if `[ -d "$old/.git" ]`** — exactly your guard |
| `pitfalls/chezmoi-update-blesh-local-changes-overwritten.md` (new) + README index row | symptom-titled, verbatim error |
| `docs/zsh/oh-my-zsh-plugins.md` | refreshed stale line-ref `105-112`→`114-121` |

**Verified end-to-end on this machine:**
- `~/.local/src/blesh/.git` exists (clean source); `~/.local/share/blesh/.git` gone (plain runtime).
- Runtime `ble.sh` built fresh — `_ble_init_version=0.4.0-devel4+f38850c`, matching the source HEAD `f38850c`.
- **The regression op** (`chezmoi apply --refresh-externals`) now returns `Already up to date.` and the source clone stays clean — the dirty-tree pull block is gone.

**Caveats, stated honestly:**
- I could **not** PTY-verify interactive ble.sh *attach* (the Bash tool has no terminal, and ble.sh bails without one). The `make install` command is byte-identical to before and `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is untouched, so attach behavior is unchanged — but I didn't observe it loading in a live shell.
- `mkdocs build --strict` aborts on **pre-existing** anchor drift (`tmux/*.zh-TW.md` + `llmstxt` plugin, tracked in `backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md`); none of the 11 warnings touch my edits.
- On this box I ran the migration + install scripts directly (via `chezmoi execute-template | bash`) to avoid a full apply reverting your **unrelated in-flight drift** (`~/.ansible/.../coding_agents`, `.visidatarc`). On other hosts the committed scripts run automatically on next `chezmoi update`.

I left untouched the unrelated pending work (`opencodebox-wrapper` TODO/backlog entries, `.antigravitycli/`) and did **not** commit anything. Want me to commit just the blesh fix's files?
